title: Review of Misuse of Drugs Act
what_it_is: Review of Misuse of Drugs Act

sections.label: Adili charged with importing methamphetamine
sections.summary: Adili Chibuike Ejike was charged with importing almost two kilogrammes of methamphetamine into Singapore, and the passage sets out the elements of importing under section 7 of the Misuse of Drugs Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Adili Chibuike Ejike was charged with importing almost two kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine, commonly known as "Ice" into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: A person will be guilty of importing under section 7 of the Misuse of Drugs Act (MDA) if: (a) he is in possession of the drugs; (b) knew of their presence and their nature; and (c) brought the drugs into Singapore without prior authorisation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: When these presumptions apply, a person charged with importing prohibited drugs can be presumed to know of their presence, as well as their nature.

sections.label: Prosecution conceded Adili lacked knowledge
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal noted the prosecution conceded Adili did not actually know of the drugs' presence, so the presumption cannot apply.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Court of Appeal noted that the prosecution, in their cross-examination of Adili and in their arguments in addressing this issue, had conceded that Adili did not actually know of the presence of the drugs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Members will appreciate, once the prosecution accepts that the accused did not know of the presence of the drugs, then the presumption cannot apply.

sections.label: Government studying willful blindness observations
sections.summary: The Government is studying the Court of Appeal's observations on willful blindness and will set out its views and whether legislative amendments are necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: There are other observations made by the Court of Appeal on willful blindness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We are studying those observations carefully and will set out the Government's views in due course, and whether any legislative amendments are necessary.

sections.label: Well-hidden drugs and presumptions
sections.summary: The fact alone that the drugs were well-hidden would not cause the presumptions to be rebutted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The fact alone that the drugs were well-hidden would not cause the presumptions to be rebutted.

sections.label: Adili's case turns on facts
sections.summary: The outcome of each case depends on its unique facts and circumstances and the evidence, and Adili's case turns on its facts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The outcome of each case depends on its unique facts and circumstances as well as the evidence, and Adili's case turns on its facts.
